sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Launch Vehicle**: Launched using **PSLV-C25** (XL version), which is a four-stage rocket, not a GSLV.
• **Mission Objective**: To explore Martian surface features, morphology, mineralogy, and the Martian atmosphere (specifically Methane detection).
• **Orbital Strategy**: Utilized **Hohmann Transfer Orbit** to minimize fuel consumption by performing a series of Earth-bound maneuvers before the Trans-Mars Injection (TMI).
• **Key Metric**: The mission was completed in a record time of ~15 months from project approval to launch, with a cost of ~₹450 Crore ($74 million).

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Technological Demonstration**: Proved India's capability in deep-space navigation and autonomous mission control.
• **Scientific Data**: Provided high-resolution imagery of Mars's surface and data on dust storms.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Communication latency (up to 20 mins), harsh radiation environment, and limited power supply.
• **Solutions**: Mangalyaan-2 (MOM-2) is planned with advanced payloads and a lander/rover component.

items.title: Mnemonic for Payloads
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'M-T-M-M-L' (My Tiny Mars Mission Lands)
• **Decoded**: MCC, TIS, MSM, MENCA, Lyman Alpha Photometer.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often claims MOM was launched by GSLV. It was launched by PSLV-C25. Also, it was an Orbiter mission, NOT a Lander/Rover mission.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Frugal Engineering' to describe ISRO's cost-effective approach to space exploration.

keyTakeaways: India is the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit and the first in the world to do so on its maiden attempt.
The mission utilized the PSLV-C25 launch vehicle, emphasizing the reliability of the PSLV platform.
MOM-1 was primarily a technology demonstrator mission, paving the way for future complex interplanetary missions.
